title: GS21 industry sign x financial leverage with a continuous firm-level debt capacity: six mirrored types on the gs_level ladder, exposure gs_bv_f x coupon/0.40 (gs_bzl 1.25, gs_bzc 0.725), coupons drawn from [0.1, 0.9], price 2.5
question: Does an interaction with a plain story (industries on opposite sides of a priced shock, the levered firm's cash flow moving more) give GS21 room and a fair gap at the bar when leverage varies continuously across firms?
notes:
WHY (2026-11-02). The industry sign x financial leverage interaction with a firm-level, continuously drawn debt capacity (gs_fixcs 2, coupon from the 16 grid nodes in [0.1, 0.9], fixed for life). The fixed-coupon TYPE version (gvysl15/20) had room under 1% because two industries x three coupons are six perfectly observed groups the linear model prices directly. Six mirrored industry types on the gs_level ladder 0.5..2.0 (size reveals the sign in part), no compensation. The exposure is gs_bv_f x (1.25 + 0.725 b~) = gs_bv_f x coupon/0.40: proportional to the coupon, the same sign within an industry (the levered firm's cash flow moves more). Loadings [-0.15, -0.1, -0.05, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15].

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false; ids filled from the Quest build log by the solve script before any seed runs.

PREDICTION (2026-11-02): room 30% or more (gvysz2, the same construction on productivity: 22-66%) and a fair gap at or above +0.029. FALSIFIED if room is at or below 10% on three seeds.
